target: DUM-E concurrency architecture (Serve/Train split + windowed coalescing), CONCURRENCY_DESIGN.md, reviewed against trainer.py / training.py / db.py / main.py

holes.issue: The Server's read path can reintroduce the exact corruption that forced max_inputs=1, because reads mutate self.model in MORE places than the doc accounts for.
holes.why: The doc (§2, §6) claims the max_inputs=1 premise is purely a 'serialize readers' rationale and that dropping the in-place mutation from the happy full-checkpoint path makes max_inputs>1 safe. But _load_current_model mutates shared state on EVERY non-happy branch: the no-version branch calls self._reset_base() and returns self.model (trainer.py:962-963); the full-load FAILURE branch calls self._reset_base() and returns self.model (trainer.py:979-980); the legacy branch does self._reset_base() + self.model = PeftModel(...).merge_and_unload() (trainer.py:993-1003). _reset_base() does self.model.load_state_dict(...) in place (trainer.py:363). Under max_inputs=6, two concurrent calls where ANY hits a fallback (Modal reload flake, a half-written v{N}, a transient from_pretrained OOM, or simply CURRENT unset at cold start before the first flip) race a load_state_dict against another call's forward pass on the same self.model = garbage output or hard crash. The design only removes the mutation from the one path that already worked; the fallbacks it keeps are the corruption vector.
holes.fix: Rewrite the Server read path to be TRULY immutable: never touch self.model/self._reset_base in generation. Keep an always-resident self.base_model built once in load() and NEVER mutated, plus an immutable self._served_model cache. Every fallback (no version, load fail, legacy) must resolve to a locally-scoped module reference returned to the caller, never an assignment to a shared attribute. Delete the legacy adapter branch from Server entirely (doc already says to, but it currently still self.model=merge_and_unload). Add an assertion/test that no Server code path assigns self.model or calls _reset_base.

holes.issue: _refresh_current has no in-replica lock, so up to max_inputs=6 concurrent calls on one replica all detect the moved pointer and simultaneously from_pretrained the new full checkpoint, multiplying GPU memory and load work -> A10G OOM on every flip.
holes.why: The sketch (§2 lines 111-125, 128-131) calls self._refresh_current() at the top of EVERY generate_stream, unconditionally, with no guard. With @concurrent(max_inputs=6), right after a flip all 6 in-flight/incoming calls on a replica read the new pointer, all see version != self._current_version, and all enter _materialize -> 6x AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained of a full 1B bf16 checkpoint at once. That is ~6x transient GPU memory plus 6x load latency precisely at the moment min_containers=2 was supposed to make flips seamless. This is a NEW failure mode the split introduces; today max_inputs=1 makes it impossible. It also makes the 'staleness <= one vol.reload()' and 'no gap' claims false during the reload window.
holes.fix: Serialize the refresh with an asyncio.Lock/threading.Lock per replica: only the first caller loads the new checkpoint; concurrent callers either serve the still-valid OLD cached model (bounded extra staleness, which is fine) or await the single in-flight load. Also gate the reload frequency (e.g. reload at most every N ms) so vol.reload() isn't hit on literally every token-stream start under load. Document that during a post-flip load, that replica keeps serving the previous brain rather than blocking or reloading N times.

holes.issue: The 'union coalescing = same ~28s' wait-time math ignores that a 400-pair capped union + 150-pair replay + anchors cannot train to convergence within MAX_TRAIN_SECONDS=25s, so lessons in a large window may not stick.
holes.why: The trainer bounds work by wall-clock (trainer.py:592) precisely because a flat step cap starved large lessons (trainer.py:58-64). A single-lesson job today trains ~8 pairs + up to 150 replay for full epochs within 25s. A coalesced union of COALESCE_MAX_PAIRS=400 new pairs PLUS build_replay_buffer(union) up to REPLAY_BUFFER_MAX=150 PLUS anchors = ~550+ examples over 6 epochs = ~3300 example-slots. At batch 16 that's ~206 steps; the 25s budget will cut this off well before full epochs, so EACH pair is seen <1x -- the exact undertraining the code comments warn against. So the honest outcome for a 50-teacher burst is not '50 lessons all live and learned in 28s' but 'one undertrained checkpoint where many lessons barely moved the weights.' The table conflates 'a checkpoint exists' with 'the lesson was learned.'
holes.fix: State the real tradeoff: coalescing trades depth-latency for per-lesson training strength under a fixed time box. Either (a) scale MAX_TRAIN_SECONDS with batch size for coalesced windows (compute is explicitly not a constraint), or (b) cap COALESCE_MAX_PAIRS far lower (~64) and accept 2-4 windows for 50 teachers (~1-2 min, still vs 23 min), or (c) drop/shrink the replay buffer for coalesced windows since the union already contains many concurrent lessons. Re-derive the table with a realistic pairs-vs-time budget; do not claim 28s covers 400 pairs.

holes.issue: Two contradictory concurrent lessons in the SAME union do NOT resolve by 'later/more-frequent dominates' -- within one shuffled batch there is no 'later,' so the outcome is the smeared average the doc claims only B (TIES) suffers.
holes.why: §3 argues union-SGD resolves 1+1=3 vs 1+1=5 'the way the product already relies on (later/more-frequent pairs dominate).' That reliance holds for SEQUENTIAL lessons (a later job trains on a checkpoint that already learned the earlier one). But coalescing puts both contradictory pair-sets into ONE DataLoader with shuffle=True (trainer.py:550) trained jointly to the same optimum. Two mutually-exclusive targets for the same prompt in one batch produce gradient cancellation toward a blended distribution over {3,5} -- i.e. exactly the 'degraded average' the doc attributes to B and claims D avoids. Whichever has more pairs wins only probabilistically, and neither may sit at 1.0. This contradicts the design's own stated advantage over B and is invariant-relevant: it changes what 'the one shared brain learned' actually is versus the sequential path it's replacing.
holes.fix: Acknowledge that coalescing changes contradiction-resolution semantics from sequential-last-wins to joint-optimization-blend, and decide that's acceptable per invariant (a) (incoherent is fine) OR preserve last-wins by ordering: within a window, dedupe contradictory prompts keeping only the highest-lesson-id pair per prompt before unioning, so the newest teach for a given prompt wins deterministically. Don't claim D resolves contradictions 'the way the product already relies on' -- it demonstrably doesn't for same-window collisions.

holes.issue: claim_next_batch draining ALL queued lessons in a 4s window opens a starvation/monopolization hole and a batch-poison amplification the per-job design didn't have.
holes.why: Draining the window into ONE finetune means one lesson that triggers an OOM/NaN (e.g. a pathologically long pair that blows MAX_SEQ_LEN batching) fails the WHOLE batch. §5's mitigation ('requeue each lesson individually once') means a 40-lesson poisoned batch degrades to 40 individual jobs -- i.e. it falls back to exactly the 23-minute FIFO the design exists to prevent, and does so precisely under the adversarial/load conditions that matter. Also, because the collector drains everything queued, a steady high arrival rate never lets the window close small: it keeps sweeping in newly-arrived lessons up to the caps, so 'position 1, ~28s' can actually be 'position 1' forever while the effective batch keeps growing to the cap and each teacher waits the full window+train repeatedly.
holes.fix: Bound batch formation by a HARD cutoff timestamp captured at window open (only lessons queued before T0 join this batch; later arrivals wait for the next window), so a batch can't grow unboundedly under sustained load. For poison isolation, prefer bisection/quarantine over full fan-out-to-singles: on batch failure, split the batch in half and retry halves (log2 passes) rather than N sequential singles, so one poison lesson costs ~log(N) windows not N.

holes.issue: The startup DB<->Volume reconciliation (main.py:74) and the DB is_current mirror are single-writer assumptions that the doc keeps, but coalescing writes new_weights_version/set_current_weights from the SAME single worker -- fine -- yet the doc also proposes uvicorn --workers>1 + busy_timeout, which reintroduces multiple worker LOOPS each running claim_next_batch.
holes.why: The doc simultaneously (a) relies on 'single worker loop' for the flip being non-concurrent and (b) recommends busy_timeout PRAGMA 'for --workers>1' (§5, §6 db.py). If you actually run uvicorn with >1 worker, EACH process runs its own _worker_loop and its own claim_next_batch. BEGIN IMMEDIATE makes the CLAIM atomic (only one worker claims a given batch), which is correct -- BUT two workers can now claim two DISJOINT batches concurrently and both call Trainer.finetune.remote. Modal's max_containers=1/max_inputs=1 serializes them on the data plane, so worker A's finetune and worker B's finetune run back-to-back; but each resolved its base_version snapshot independently at claim time. Worker B claimed while A's finetune was in flight (not yet flipped), so B's base_version is the PRE-A checkpoint -> B trains on stale base -> B's flip silently drops A's lessons (lost update). The doc's 'snapshot-once under the claim' protects within one worker but not across two worker loops racing the flip. Today this is masked because one job runs to completion (flip included) before the next claim; batching doesn't change that, but explicitly endorsing --workers>1 does.
holes.fix: Either forbid >1 worker LOOP (keep the loop single-instance even if uvicorn has multiple web workers -- gate the loop behind a DB-advisory single-owner lease, not just the per-claim BEGIN IMMEDIATE), OR make base_version resolution + flip a true critical section spanning the whole train (a writer lease row held for the batch duration, released on flip), so a second worker cannot claim-and-train against a base that's about to be superseded. The busy_timeout note is fine for web reads but must not be read as 'multiple training loops are safe.'

holes.issue: vol.commit()/vol.reload() semantics: readers can observe a moved CURRENT pointer BEFORE the v{N+1} directory contents are visible on their replica, because commit and the reader's reload are independent.
holes.why: §4.3 asserts 'readers that reload mid-save either see old pointer or the new pointer after the new dir is fully written.' That's true within the WRITER container's filesystem, but Server replicas are DIFFERENT containers that only see writes after their own vol.reload() pulls the committed snapshot. Modal Volume reload pulls a consistent committed snapshot, so if the writer does save_pretrained -> _flip_current -> vol.commit() as ONE commit, a reader reload sees all-or-nothing. BUT trainer.py TODAY commits once at end (vol.commit() line 648) after _flip_current -- good. The risk the doc introduces: if the Server calls vol.reload() and reads CURRENT=vN+1 but the from_pretrained of /weights/vN+1 races a partial local materialization, or if there's any window where the pointer is committed in a separate commit from the dir. The doc must pin that pointer-flip and dir-write land in the SAME vol.commit() and that Server never reads CURRENT except immediately after a successful reload of that same commit.
holes.fix: Make it explicit and enforced: writer writes v{N+1} dir, flips CURRENT, then a SINGLE vol.commit() (as trainer.py:646-648 already does -- don't split it). Server _refresh_current must read CURRENT only from the just-reloaded snapshot (never a stale os.read from before reload). Add a guard: if _read_current() names a dir that isn't present/complete on the reloaded volume (missing config.json/safetensors), treat as 'pointer moved but not yet visible' and keep serving the cached model rather than failing the load -- this also covers the transient where reload lands the pointer before the large weight shards on a slow pull.

holes.issue: Removing generate/generate_stream from Trainer breaks warmup(), _generate_remote(), infer_chat(), and reset flows that call Trainer directly -- the migration section undercounts the call sites.
holes.why: §6 says 'repoint infer_chat_stream/infer_chat/infer from Trainer to Server.' But warmup() (training.py:175-196) calls Trainer().generate to warm the container -- after the split, warming the Trainer no longer warms the Server pool that actually serves chat, so the first real chat pays a Server cold start the warmup was meant to hide (concern #9 regression). Also reset() local_entrypoint calls Trainer().reset_memory (trainer.py:1132) and reset_remote() resets Trainer's memory -- but after the split the SERVER replicas hold their own cached self._served_model, which a Trainer-only reset does NOT clear, so a post-reset Server keeps answering as taught until scaledown. The doc's reset story is now split-brained.
holes.fix: Point warmup() at Server (fire a 1-token Server.generate to warm a replica; consider warming >=min_containers). Add a Server.reset/refresh path (or have reset flip CURRENT to a base sentinel and rely on _refresh_current) so POST /api/admin/reset actually forgets on the read replicas, not just the writer. Enumerate ALL Trainer.generate* call sites (warmup, _generate_remote, infer, infer_chat, infer_chat_stream) in the migration.

holes.issue: The claim-lease reaper using claimed_at with TTL=2xMAX_TRAIN_SECONDS is too short for coalesced/consolidation jobs and will reap live batches.
holes.why: §5 sets the lease TTL at ~2xMAX_TRAIN_SECONDS (=50s) but a coalesced batch legitimately runs up to MAX_TRAIN_SECONDS + save/flip, and CONSOLIDATE_MAX_SECONDS is 180s (trainer.py:127). A reaper with a 50s TTL will declare a healthy in-flight consolidation (or a batch that hit a Modal cold start of ~30-60s + 25s train) as stale and requeue it, causing a duplicate concurrent train of the same lessons -> two flips -> lost update / churn. Cold starts alone can exceed 50s.
holes.fix: Set the lease TTL from the job's OWN budget: max(MAX_TRAIN_SECONDS, CONSOLIDATE_MAX_SECONDS) + a cold-start allowance (e.g. +120s), or heartbeat claimed_at during training so a live-but-slow job isn't reaped. Never use a single global 2x constant that's blind to consolidation and cold starts.

target: Adversarial validity review of E1–E4 (fullft-vs-lora, core-parroting, latency-seqlen, prior-leakage) as run in /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/{e1_fullft_vs_lora.py, e2_parroting.py, e3_sweep.py, e4_leakage.py}, metrics.py, data.py, and the e1_run.log / e2_results.json / e4_results.json outputs.

holes.issue: E1's headline verdict ('full-FT buys ZERO quality/retention improvement over LoRA') rests on saturated ceiling metrics that cannot resolve any difference. Every one of the 4 arms returns retention=1.0, coherence=0.96, arbitrary_learn=1.0, and the identical string '1 + 1 = 3.' The instruments are: retention = substring match ('Paris','4','red'); coherence_score (metrics.py:47) = unique-word ratio with a <3-word floor. Both max out on any converged 1B model over a 5-probe / 3-probe eval regardless of training method.
holes.why: The experiment's core DECISION ('full does not beat LoRA, do not change the method for quality reasons') is stated as design-grade, but a null result produced by every arm hitting the metric ceiling is not evidence of equivalence — it is evidence the eval is too blunt to detect a difference. The one caveat buried at the end ('metrics saturated ... cannot distinguish fine-grained quality') actually invalidates the headline, which the verdict then still asserts. A real chat-quality difference (fluency, instruction-following, multi-turn coherence) would be completely invisible here.
holes.fix: Re-run E1 with (a) an LLM-judge or perplexity-on-held-out-chat metric that is NOT at ceiling, over 30-50 diverse retention/chat prompts (not 5), and (b) MMLU-style or a small held-out instruction set to catch capability erosion. Only if a non-saturated metric still shows parity can 'zero improvement' be trusted. Until then treat E1's fit/VRAM/timing numbers as valid but the quality verdict as UNRESOLVED.

holes.issue: E1 retention is measured on prompts that are IN the training corpus. _build_corpus (e1_fullft_vs_lora.py:66-67) augments RETENTION_PROBES prompts into the corpus (the 'retention anchors'), then eval scores retention on those same RETENTION_PROBES prompts (line 229). It is train-on-test, not held-out retention.
holes.why: retention=1.0 across all arms is therefore memorization of trained prompts, not preserved general capability. The whole point of a retention probe — does the edit collapse UNRELATED ability — is defeated. This also means E1 cannot speak to catastrophic forgetting at all, yet the verdict cites retention=1.0 as evidence full-FT is 'safe.'
holes.fix: Retention/anchor prompts used for EVAL must be disjoint from the prompts placed in the corpus. Use a separate held-out retention battery (different facts entirely) that never appears in training, worded differently, and re-check whether full-FT vs LoRA differ on it.

holes.issue: E1's dismissal of the 0.667 fact_flip split as 'the known metric artifact, split across methods not along the method axis' is confounded and asserted without evidence. The actual split is: a_lora=1.0, b_full_naive=1.0, c_full_ckpt8bit=0.667, d_full_a100=0.667. The two 0.667 arms are precisely the two that differ from naive-full (8bit optimizer / A100 hardware). With only 3 fact probes and no seed replication, 0.667 vs 1.0 is a single probe flipping.
holes.why: The verdict uses this dismissal to preserve the 'all arms tied' story. But the data are equally consistent with a real (small) effect of AdamW8bit or the A100 numerics on how hard the fact sticks. n=3 probes, single run, no seeds means neither 'artifact/noise' nor 'real effect' is distinguishable — so calling it noise is an unsupported choice that happens to support the desired conclusion.
holes.fix: Re-run the 4 arms with >=3 seeds each and a larger fact-probe set (>=10 held-out phrasings, negation-aware fact metric per E2). Report per-arm mean +/- across seeds. Only then is 'no method-axis effect' a claim, not an assertion.

holes.issue: E4's 'PATCHED+scrub residual = 0 in ALL conditions' is a true-but-misleading measurement. scrubbed_leaks counts has_leak(scrub(resp)) (e4_leakage.py:57, ~line 200), i.e. it checks whether the regex still matches AFTER the regex deleted its own matches — which is 0 by construction. It does NOT verify the scrubbed pair is usable. The results even show 'who made you' at leak_rate 0.83 under PATCH still emitting 'I was created by Google.' which the scrub turns into 'I was created by .'
holes.why: The verdict leans on 'regex scrub is the reliable backstop (residual=0 everywhere)' to claim the fix works. But residual=0 is tautological for a substitution scrub and says nothing about whether the training data is now correct or grammatical. The results' own caveat ('substitution leaves broken sentences; a DROP-THE-PAIR scrub is needed') contradicts the clean 'residual=0' framing. As measured, the scrub 'succeeds' by producing broken training targets, which would poison identity lessons in a different way.
holes.fix: Re-score the scrub with a DROP-the-pair policy and report (i) how many pairs survive, (ii) grammaticality/on-concept rate of survivors, not just regex-rematch=0. The real question is 'after scrubbing, how many usable non-leaking identity pairs remain,' which was never measured.

holes.issue: E2 sample sizes are tiny and the two 'runs' are not independent seeds. held_out_flip is 8 probes, contrastive 6 probes, style 3 probes, per arm, and e2_results.json contains a single run (the prose claims 'mean of 2 runs' but only one result file exists and the finetune uses no fixed seed / shuffle=True). A 0.333->0.667->1.0 contrastive_robustness 'trend' is 2/6 -> 4/6 -> 6/6 probes — i.e. moving 2 and 4 individual probe outcomes.
holes.why: The decisive E2 claim ('contrastive pairs raise contrastive_robustness 0.33->1.0 for free') is drawn from at most 2 unseeded runs over 6 probes. Greedy decoding removes sampling noise within a run, but run-to-run LoRA training variance (data shuffle, nondeterministic CUDA) is not characterized. A 6-probe metric moving by 2-4 hits is well within plausible train-noise, so the magnitude of the 'win' is not trustworthy even if its direction is plausible.
holes.fix: Run >=5 seeds per arm (fresh model + reshuffle), report contrastive_robustness mean +/- std and a simple test that C>A survives the variance. Expand the contrastive/held-out batteries to >=15 probes each. The direction may well hold, but the '0.33->1.0, free' framing needs the spread.

holes.issue: E2's parrot_rate metric is defined so that the baseline is already at the floor, making the pre-registered SUCCESS gate unfalsifiable, and this is treated as a finding rather than a metric failure. parrot_rate = frac(held-out gens with >=0.9 token-Jaccard to any training response). Held-out probes are deliberately long, novel-worded sentences (corpora.json held_out_flip), while training responses are short ('1 + 1 = 3.'), so Jaccard >=0.9 is nearly impossible by construction -> parrot_rate ~0 for ALL arms including HIGH-CORE.
holes.why: The experiment's stated question ('does CORE-repetition cause phrase-level parroting') is answered 'no' — but the metric could not have detected parroting even if it existed, because the held-out probes share almost no tokens with the short training answers regardless of memorization. So 'parroting refuted' is an artifact of an insensitive metric, not evidence. The verdict half-acknowledges this ('gate un-meetable because A is at the 0.0 floor') but still reports 'parroting mechanism REFUTED.'
holes.fix: Measure parroting with a sensitive probe: include held-out prompts whose IDEAL answer is short (so a memorized wrapper CAN match), or measure verbatim-substring reuse of training wrapper phrases, or exact-match rate, at a threshold that is achievable. Then 'no parroting' becomes a real negative rather than a definitional one.

holes.issue: E3's central alarming claim ('batch 16 at the padded cap OOMs at 512 already, because logits.float() over the 128k vocab is the bottleneck') is measured with a pathological synthetic corpus that does not match the padding behavior of the real trainer, and is over-generalized. e3_sweep.py:172-175 makes every one of 150 pairs a ~600-token prompt + ~200-repeat response, all identical, so build_examples truncates each to exactly max_seq_len and collate pads the whole batch to the cap. The realistic arm (short pairs) shows flat 6.6GB with cap never binding.
holes.why: The OOM is real for the constructed worst case, and the token-budgeting recommendation is sound. But the framing 'MAX_SEQ_LEN 512->1024 does NOT stay well under 24GB at batch 16 — OOMs at 512' reads as a property of the cap, when it is a property of a fully-padded 512-token batch that the real workload never produces (real lessons are short; the production collate pads to batch-max, not to the cap). The severity/likelihood of this failure in production is overstated by the synthetic setup, though the mitigation is still worth doing.
holes.fix: Keep the recommendation (token-budgeted batching) but re-label the finding as 'pathological long-lesson worst case,' and measure the ACTUAL distribution of production pair lengths to estimate how often a batch approaches the OOM regime. Also confirm the real trainer pads to batch-max (dynamic) not to the fixed cap, which changes the risk substantially.

holes.issue: Across all four experiments there is no seed replication and no variance reporting; every headline number is a point estimate from a single training run per arm (E1 1 run/arm, E2 nominally 2 but 1 result file, E3 3 reps but only for timing/VRAM not quality, E4 1 generation batch/condition).
holes.why: Multiple load-bearing verdicts ('full ties LoRA', 'contrast is free', 'stronger persona line hits 0.074') are differences between single-run point estimates on <=8-probe metrics. Without run-to-run spread there is no way to know which gaps exceed noise. This is exactly the failure mode the project's own memory flags (the 0.667 'wall' that turned out to be a metric artifact), so the bar for seed replication should be high here specifically.
holes.fix: For any number used to make a design decision, run >=3-5 seeds and report mean +/- std (or min/max). Flag any verdict whose claimed gap is smaller than the observed cross-seed spread as UNRESOLVED.
